entries.subject:
Primary request: early sulfuric-acid manufacture represented by a single small lead chamber, inspired by eighteenth-century batch apparatus, NOT modern towers or a glass laboratory still.
Subject: a stout, nearly cubical box made of warm-neutral grey sheet lead, supported by a simple compact brown timber skeleton integral to the apparatus. Flat roof, clearly folded metal seams, no decorative rivet overload. The front-left part of the wall is omitted as a clean explanatory cutaway, revealing the lead-lined chamber, a shallow pale transparent liquid layer along its bottom and a small low iron burning tray with a few subdued yellow sulfur pieces above the liquid. Keep the box visually dominant and its boundaries mechanically coherent; metal sheet walls have thickness, no floating fragments. The open section is an interior cavity, not an exterior black fill. A closed right wall and intact back wall make the box shape obvious. Short support legs with genuine empty space underneath, no platform or ground plane.
One small clear glass receiver bottle is the sole accessory at the lower right, lightly filled with colorless liquid, plain cork, no label. Make it subordinate. Keep the whole silhouette compact and bold, with the pale lead sheet material legible against dark UI backgrounds.
Avoid: acid pouring onto hands, corrosive fantasy neon liquid, smoke cloud, giant flame, tall chimney, Glover or Gay-Lussac tower, pipes everywhere, miniature factory, pitched-roof house, large boiler, round copper alembic, pressure gauge, modern stainless tanks. No scene. The chamber cutaway is a simplified symbol of manufacture rather than an operating installation.

entries.subject:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset type: revised TECHNOLOGY icon for Victoria 3, Alcalis industriels.
Input images: Image 1 is the EDIT TARGET. Make a targeted correction to the RIGHT END OF THE FURNACE AND ITS CHIMNEY ONLY.
Primary request: the chimney must clearly connect to the furnace INTERIOR. The working chamber currently appears to stop before the chimney. Extend the same brick working chamber to meet an integrated flue at the right end, so there is NO disconnected chimney and NO solid end wall blocking the exhaust.
Correction: put the squat chimney directly at the terminal right end of the continuous masonry body. Its base continues down into an attached masonry flue neck that touches the working hearth. Use a SMALL intentional explanatory cutaway in the FRONT FACE of this right-end neck, revealing one clear continuous dark L-SHAPED passage: it enters horizontally from the existing working cavity, then turns UPWARD inside the chimney, ending at the chimney's visible open top. This is one connected hollow gas passage, not a decorative groove or a crack. The right end of the chamber opens into this flue, not against solid brick. The chimney walls have coherent thickness. Keep the cutaway compact and integral to the furnace, no detached diagram, arrows, x-ray glow, tubes, floating bricks or extra pipe networks. Both the interior passage and external masonry connection should be readable without labels.
Invariants: keep the rest of the low stationary reverberatory furnace unchanged: same brick color and courses, broad working arch, iron ties, left firebox, open iron door, restrained warm firelight inside, dark granular hearth, and the single lower-right tray of white soda ash. Same viewpoint, scale and painted matte texture. Do not redesign the whole furnace, add a taller chimney, a rotary drum, a second firebox, new equipment or accessories.
Scene/backdrop: preserve genuine transparent alpha outside the object. Empty background and exterior gaps stay transparent, not black painted pixels or a brown glow. The dark flue is a physical interior cavity, not exterior transparency. No floor or ground shadow, scene, UI frame, medallion, text or watermark.
Composition: centered SQUARE canvas at least 1024 pixels, complete silhouette and tray intact, generous transparent margins. Preserve natural terracotta, warm-neutral grey iron and white powder; no global blue cast. Readable at 48 and 64 pixels. Stylized explanatory cutaway, not a certified engineering drawing.

entries.subject:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset type: revised TECHNOLOGY icon for Victoria 3, Céramique industrielle.
Input images: Image 1 is the EDIT TARGET. Replace its entire saggar-and-bowl subject, but keep the compact hand-painted volumetric technology-icon style, matte material treatment and soft upper-left illumination.
Primary request: show SEVERAL IDENTICAL POTS MADE USING THE SAME MOULD, so standardized ceramic manufacture is immediately clear.
Subject: THREE identical simple handleless ceramic jars of exactly the same form and size, made in the same mould. Each has a rounded slightly bulbous belly, a short wide neck, a plain gently flared open lip and a small flat base. All three use the same clean ivory-white material, matching proportions and restrained smooth finish, no decoration, different shapes or mismatched rim sizes. Arrange them in one compact readable group with their matching contours and all three separate open mouths visible. They are standing finished vessels, not bowls nested inside each other.
One common reusable two-part PLASTER MOULD is the single supporting accessory: place its two separated halves together just behind the group, with a plainly visible concave negative cavity EXACTLY MATCHING the same jar silhouette and dimensions. The two halves are parts of ONE mould, not two different moulds. Rough matte pale warm-grey/buff plaster, simple mould blocks, a coherent vertical parting plane and a few modest integral registration sockets. Clearly concave inner profiles, not jars stuck onto the mould faces. No green plastic pins or modern machine components.
Scene/backdrop: genuine transparent alpha around the complete isolated group and in exterior gaps. No table, surface, floor, ground shadow, scene, painted black/white background, checkerboard, pedestal, UI frame or medallion. Shadows belong ON the objects only.
Composition: square canvas at least 1024 pixels, modest three-quarter view, all pieces completely within the canvas with generous transparent margins. Three repeated pots are the dominant homogeneous group; the one opened mould supports the concept. Broad legible masses at 48/64 pixels, not tiny workshop details.
Invariants: preserve the existing vanilla-like brushed painted volume and natural neutral color balance. Ivory pots and rough neutral plaster must remain distinguishable. No blue/teal cast, gold ornaments, glossy 3D, photorealistic workshop, people, labels, text, arrows, watermark, extra tools or accessories.
Remove the old firing cassette, the single bowl and the kiln motifs entirely. This is a simplified historical-style depiction of mould-based serial production, not a certified replica of a particular dated mould.
